source_text: τὸν πρὸ πάντων ὄντα καὶ πάσης φύσεως ὑπερφυῶς ἐπιτροπεύοντα μηδὲν εἶναι τῶν πάντων, 15.97 μηδὲ κτίσμα κατὰ σύγκρισιν νοεῖσθαι τῶν παρ' αὐτοῦ παροισθέντων 13 καὶ πᾶσαν εἰληχότων πρὸς αὐτὸν ἐξαλλαγήν. 15.98 καὶ ἄλλως· ὃν ἄν τις παντὸς ποιήματος ποιητὴν ἀποφήναιτο καὶ πᾶσαν βαστάζοντα τὴν κτίσιν καὶ εἰκόνα τοῦ θεοῦ καὶ υἱὸν ὀνομάσοι, τῇ τε ἀληθείᾳ προσέχων καὶ ὑπὸ τῶν θείων λογίων πληροφορούμενος, τοῦτον πῶς ἂν ποίημα ἢ μικρότερον τοῦ φέροντος τὰ πάντα θεοῦ ἢ προγενέστερον ἔχοντα, εἰ μὴ μαίνοιτο, προσομολογήσοι; 15.99 Περὶ δὲ τοῦ θεὸν καὶ ἄγγελον κεκλῆσθαι προφητεύουσιν Μαλαχίας μὲν οὕτως εἰπών· «ἥξει εἰς τὸν ναὸν αὐτοῦ κύριος, ὃν ὑμεῖς ζητεῖτε, καὶ ὁ ἄγγελος τῆς διαθή κης, ὃν ὑμεῖς θέλετε. ἰδοὺ ἔρχεται κύριος, καὶ τίς ὑπομενεῖ ἡμέραν εἰσόδου αὐτοῦ; ἢ τίς ὑποστήσεται ἐν τῇ ὀπτασίᾳ αὐτοῦ;» 15.100 ἡ ἀρχὴ τοῦ ῥητοῦ τὴν οἰκονομίαν, τὸ δὲ ἑπόμενον τὴν φοβερὰν καὶ φιλάνθρωπον αὐτοῦ δευτέραν παρουσίαν δηλοῖ. 15.101 Ἠσαΐας δὲ βοῶν τρόπῳ ᾧ εἰώθασιν οἱ συγχαίροντες ἀγγέλλειν τοῖς οὔπω τοῦ γενομένου ᾐσθημένοις· «παιδίον ἐγεννήθη ἡμῖν, υἱὸς καὶ ἐδόθη, καὶ καλεῖται τὸ ὄνομα αὐτοῦ μεγά λης βουλῆς ἄγγελος, θαυμαστὸς σύμβουλος, θεὸς ἰσχυρός, ἐξουσιαστής, ἄρχων εἰρήνης». 15.102 Τοῦτον τὸν θεὸν λόγον καὶ Ἰακὼβ ἄγγελον καλεῖ, ὅτε πορευόμενος εἰς Μεσοποταμίαν κοιμηθεὶς εἶδεν ὄναρ. φησὶν γάρ· «καὶ ἰδοῦ κλίμαξ ἐστηριγμένη ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς, ἧς ἡ κεφαλὴ ἐφικνεῖτο εἰς τὸν οὐρανόν. καὶ οἱ ἄγγελοι τοῦ θεοῦ ἀνέβαινον καὶ κατέβαινον ἐπ' αὐτῆς, ὁ δὲ κύριος ἐπεστήρικτο ἐπ' αὐτῆς καὶ εἶπεν· ἐγὼ κύριος ὁ θεὸς τῶν πατέρων σου, ὁ θεὸς Ἀβραὰμ καὶ ὁ θεὸς Ἰσαάκ. μὴ φοβοῦ· ἡ γῇ, ἐφ' ἧς σὺ καθεύδεις, σοὶ δώσω αὐτὴν καὶ τῷ σπέρματί σου. καὶ ἐγὼ ἔσομαι μετά σου καὶ διαφυ λάξω σε ἐν τῇ ὁδῷ πάσῃ. ᾗ ἐὰν πορευθῇς, καὶ ἀποστρέψω σε μετὰ σωτηρί ας εἰς τὸν οἶκον τοῦ πατρός σου. καὶ πλατυνθήσεται τὸ σπέρμα σου ἐπὶ λίβα καὶ θάλασσαν καὶ βορρᾶν καὶ ἀνατολάς». 15.103 Προεφητεύετο δὲ διὰ μὲν τῆς κλίμακος ὁ σταυρός, δι' οὗ οἱ πιστοὶ ἐπὶ τὰς οὐρανίους ἀναβαίνουσιν σκηνάς, ὁ δὲ ἐπὶ τῇ κλίμακι ἐπεστηριγμένος θεὸς αὐτὸς ὁ ἑκουσίως τῷ σταυρῷ ὑπὲρ ἡμῶν προσηλωθείς. 15.104 Καὶ μεθ' ἕτερα· «ηὔξατο», φησίν, «Ἰακώβ· ἐὰν ᾖ κύριος ὁ θεὸς μετ' ἐμοῦ καὶ διαφυλάξῃ με ἐν τῇ ὁδῷ, ᾖ πορεύομαι, καὶ δῷ μοι ἄρτον φαγεῖν καὶ ἱμάτιον περιβαλέσθαι καὶ ἀποστρέψῃ με μετὰ σωτηρίας εἰς τὸν οἶκον τοῦ πατρός μου, καὶ ἔσται μοι κύριος εἰς θεόν· καὶ ὁ λίθος οὗτος, ὃν ἔστησα στήλην, ἔσται μοι οἶκος θεοῦ. καὶ ἀπὸ πάντων, ὧν ἄν μοι δῷς, δεκάτην ἀποδεκατώσω σοι». 15.105 Εἶτα πληθυνθεὶς παρὰ τῷ Λάβαν εἶδεν ἐν τῇ κισσήσει τῶν θρεμμάτων πάλιν ἐν ὀπτασίᾳ τὸν ἀνωτέρω ὀφθέντα αὐτῷ θεὸν 15.106 καὶ διηγήσατο οὑτωσί· «εἶπέν μοι ὁ ἄγγελος τοῦ θεοῦ καθ' ὕπνον· Ἰακώβ, ἀνάβλεψον τοῖς ὀφθαλ μοῖς σου καὶ ἰδὲ τοὺς κριοὺς καὶ τοὺς τράγους ἀναβαίνοντας ἐπὶ τὰ πρόβατα καὶ τὰς αἶγας· οἶδα γάρ, ὅσα σοι Λάβαν ποιήσει. ἐγώ εἰμι ὁ θεὸς ὁ ὀφθείς σοι ἐν τῇ ὁδῷ, ᾗ ἤρχου, οὗ ἔστησάς μοι στήλην καὶ ηὔξω μοι ἐκεῖ εὐχήν». 15.107 Καὶ ἐν Αἰγύπτῳ δὲ ὁ αὐτὸς Ἰακὼβ τοῖς υἱοῖς Ἰωσὴφ τούτου τοῦ ἀγγέλου καὶ «μεγάλου θεοῦ» τὴν εὐλογίαν αἰτεῖται εἰπών· «ὁ θεός, ᾧ εὐηρέστησαν οἱ πατέρες μου Ἀβραὰμ καὶ Ἰσαάκ, ὁ θεὸς ὁ τρέφων με ἐκ νεότητός μου ἕως τῆς ἡμέρας ταύτης, ὁ ἄγγελος ὁ ῥυόμενός με ἐκ πάν των τῶν κακῶν μου». 16.ν Περὶ τῶν λεγόντων, ὅτι «ἀσύγκριτος καὶ μείζων ὁ πατὴρ τοῦ υἱοῦ» καὶ ὅτι «ἄλλο εἰκὼν καὶ ἄλλο θεὸς» καὶ ὅτι «καὶ ἄνθρωπος εἰκὼν θεοῦ ἐγράφη καὶ δόξα». καὶ περὶ τοῦ μαρτυρεῖσθαι κατ' οὐδὲν διαφέρειν τοῦ υἱοῦ τὸν πατέρα. 16.1 Καὶ τὸ ἀσύγκριτον δὲ καὶ μεῖζον τῷ πατρὶ διὰ τὸ ἀγέννητον ἀπονέμουσιν, τῷ δὲ υἱῷ τὸ ἀνόμοιον διὰ τὸ ἔχειν τὸ γεννητόν, καθέλκοντες πάλιν τὰ περὶ τῆς ἀρρητοτάτης θεότητος εἰς τὰ τῆς ἡμετέρας φύσεως ἀποτελέσματα καὶ τὰ
pass_a_gloss: [... it is necessary that] the one being before all things and supernaturally governing as guardian every nature be none of all things, 15.97 and not be thought a creature by comparison with the things brought forth by him and having received by lot every difference toward him. 15.98 And otherwise: the one whom someone would declare maker of every made thing and bearing the whole creation, and would name image of God and Son, both attending to the truth and fully assured by the divine oracles, how would he also confess this one to be a made thing, or smaller than the God who bears all things, or having an older-born one, unless he were raving? 15.99 And concerning his having been called God and angel, they prophesy: Malachi on the one hand speaking thus: 'the Lord whom you seek will come into his temple, and the angel of the covenant whom you wish. Look, the Lord comes, and who will endure the day of his entering? or who will stand up in his appearing?' 15.100 The beginning of the saying shows the dispensation, and the following shows his fearful and man-loving second coming. 15.101 And Isaiah, shouting in the manner in which those rejoicing with others are accustomed to announce to those not yet having perceived the thing that happened: 'a child was born to us, a son also was given, and his name is called angel of great counsel, wonderful counsellor, strong God, one holding authority, ruler of peace'. 15.102 This God Word Jacob too calls angel, when going into Mesopotamia, having fallen asleep he saw a dream. For it says: 'and look, a ladder fixed firm on the earth, whose head reached into heaven. And the angels of God were going up and going down on it, and the Lord stood fixed upon it and said: I am the Lord, the God of your fathers, the God of Abraham and the God of Isaac. Do not fear; the land on which you sleep, to you I will give it and to your seed. And I will be with you and will guard you in every way by which you go, and I will turn you back with safety into the house of your father. And your seed will be broadened toward the south-west wind and the sea and the north and the risings.' 15.103 And through the ladder was foretold the cross, through which the faithful go up to the heavenly tents, and the God fixed upon the ladder [was] himself the one willingly nailed to the cross on behalf of us. 15.104 And after other things: 'Jacob vowed,' it says: 'if the Lord God is with me and guards me in the way by which I go, and gives me bread to eat and a garment to throw around me, and turns me back with safety into the house of my father, then the Lord will be to me for God; and this stone, which I set up as a pillar, will be to me a house of God; and from all things whatever you give me, a tenth I will tithe to you'. 15.105 Then, having been multiplied with Laban, he saw at the conceiving of the flocks again in a vision the God seen by him further above, 15.106 and related thus: 'the angel of God said to me in sleep: Jacob, look up with your eyes and see the rams and the he-goats going up on the sheep and the she-goats; for I know as many things as Laban will do to you. I am the God who was seen by you in the way by which you were coming, where you set up for me a pillar and vowed to me there a vow'. 15.107 And in Egypt too the same Jacob asks for the sons of Joseph the blessing of this angel and 'great God', saying: 'the God to whom my fathers Abraham and Isaac were well-pleasing, the God who feeds me from my youth until this day, the angel who rescues me out of all my evils'. 16.ν [Chapter title:] Concerning those saying that 'incomparable and greater is the Father than the Son', and that 'image is one thing and God another', and that 'man too was written image of God and glory'; and concerning its being witnessed that the Father differs from the Son in nothing. 16.1 And incomparability and the greater they allot to the Father on account of the unbegotten, but to the Son the unlike on account of his having the begotten, dragging down again the things concerning the most unspeakable Godhead into the outcomes of our nature and the [...]
pass_b_english: … he who is before all things, and who governs every nature in a way beyond nature, should be none of all things, and should not be thought a creature by comparison with the things brought into being by him, which have received as their lot a complete difference from him.

Or to put it another way: if someone, attending to the truth and fully assured by the divine oracles, declares him the maker of everything that is made and the one who bears the whole creation, and names him the image of God and Son, how could he also confess him to be a thing made, or less than God who bears all things, or to have someone born before him, unless he were mad?

That he has been called both God and angel, the prophets foretell. Malachi says this: “The Lord whom you seek will come to his temple, and the angel of the covenant whom you desire. Behold, the Lord is coming; and who will endure the day of his entrance? Or who will stand at his appearing?” (Malachi 3:1-2). The beginning of the saying shows the saving dispensation; what follows shows his second coming, fearful and full of love for mankind.

And Isaiah cries out, in the way people who share a joy are wont to announce it to those who have not yet learned what has happened: “A child has been born to us, a son also has been given, and his name is called Angel of great counsel, Wonderful Counsellor, Mighty God, Potentate, Prince of peace” (Isaiah 9:6).

Jacob too calls this God the Word an angel, when, on his way to Mesopotamia, he fell asleep and saw a dream. For it says: “And behold, a ladder set firm on the earth, whose top reached to heaven; and the angels of God were going up and coming down on it. And the Lord stood firm upon it and said: I am the Lord, the God of your fathers, the God of Abraham and the God of Isaac. Do not fear. The land on which you are sleeping I will give to you and to your seed. And I will be with you and guard you on every way by which you go, and I will bring you back in safety to your father’s house. And your seed will spread out to the south and the west, to the north and the east” (Genesis 28:12-15).

Through the ladder the cross was foretold, by which the faithful go up to the heavenly dwellings; and the God who stood firm on the ladder is himself the one who of his own will was nailed to the cross for us.

And after other things: “Jacob vowed,” it says: “If the Lord God is with me and guards me on the way by which I go, and gives me bread to eat and a garment to put on, and brings me back in safety to my father’s house, then the Lord shall be my God; and this stone, which I have set up as a pillar, shall be to me a house of God; and of all that you give me I will give you a tenth” (Genesis 28:20-22).

Then, when he had prospered with Laban, at the time the flocks conceived (Genesis 31:10) he again saw in a vision the God who had appeared to him earlier, and he told it like this: “The angel of God said to me in my sleep: ‘Jacob, lift up your eyes and see the rams and the he-goats mounting the sheep and the she-goats; for I know all that Laban will do to you. I am the God who appeared to you on the way by which you were coming, where you set up a pillar to me and vowed a vow to me there’” (Genesis 31:11-13).

And in Egypt too the same Jacob asks this angel and “great God” for his blessing on the sons of Joseph, saying: “The God whom my fathers Abraham and Isaac pleased, the God who has fed me from my youth to this day, the angel who rescues me from all my evils” (Genesis 48:15-16).

On those who say that “the Father is incomparable and greater than the Son,” that “image is one thing and God another,” and that “man too was written to be the image and glory of God” (1 Corinthians 11:7); and on the testimony that the Father differs from the Son in nothing.

They assign incomparability and being greater to the Father because he is unbegotten, and unlikeness to the Son because he is begotten; once again they drag what concerns the most ineffable Godhead down to the conditions of our own nature and the …

choices.issue: Old draft garbled, broken and mislabelled
choices.choice: Retranslated the whole section from the Greek. The old English turned the closing clause of 15.96-15.97 into a stand-alone 'That…' statement, garbled 15.98 ('call the maker … and naming him Son'), rendered 15.99 as 'the prophecy of calling God and angel', broke Genesis 28:12-15 off at 'upon l—' and restarted it in the next paragraph with '...sea', made Jacob 'say' (ηὔξατο, he vowed) in 15.104, read ἐν τῇ κισσήσει τῶν θρεμμάτων (when the flocks conceived) as 'in the greenery of the pastures', made Jacob ask 'the sons of Joseph this angel' in 15.107, and turned the chapter title's 'the Father is incomparable and greater than the Son' into 'the Father of the Son is incomparable'. References: '(Gen 28:20-22)', '(Gen 31:11-13)', '(Gen 48:15-16)' written in full; Genesis 31:10 (the flocks conceiving) and 1 Corinthians 11:7 (man the image and glory of God) added. Bracket filler '[possessions]' removed.

choices.term: τὸν πρὸ πάντων ὄντα … μηδὲν εἶναι τῶν πάντων
choices.english: … he who is before all things … should be none of all things
choices.why: The section opens inside a sentence begun in the previous section (δεῖ γάρ, 'for it is necessary'). Only the words this section holds are translated, with a leading ellipsis; 'should' carries the sense of the infinitive after δεῖ.

choices.english: which have received as their lot a complete difference from him
choices.why: λαγχάνω 'receive by lot'; the creatures' whole being is other than his, so comparison with them cannot make him a creature.

choices.english: to have someone born before him
choices.why: The Arian claim that the Father is older than the Son; 'born before' keeps the γεν- root without adding 'the Father'.
Kept as Didymus wrote it; he uses the bearing of all things for the Son just before (πᾶσαν βαστάζοντα τὴν κτίσιν), so the point is that the Son is not less than the God whose work he shares.
Didymus' term for the incarnate economy, set against the second coming; 'saving dispensation' is the standard English sense, 'economy' would read as finance.
Paired with 'fearful': the second coming is both terrible and kind.
Didymus' argument is that Scripture calls the Son both God and angel, so 'messenger' would hide the point.
LXX Isaiah 9:5 title; 'one holding authority' as a name.

choices.term: ἐπὶ λίβα καὶ θάλασσαν καὶ βορρᾶν καὶ ἀνατολάς
choices.english: to the south and the west, to the north and the east
choices.why: In the Greek Old Testament λίψ renders the Negeb (south) and 'the sea' is the west; English names the compass points. Didymus' order (south, sea) is kept.

choices.term: ἐν τῇ ὁδῷ πάσῃ. ᾗ ἐὰν πορευθῇς
choices.english: on every way by which you go
choices.why: The copy-text's full stop inside the relative clause is a punctuation slip; read as one clause.

choices.english: then the Lord shall be my God
at the time the flocks conceived
choices.why: κίσσησις is the craving of pregnancy (LXX Genesis 31:10 ἐνεκίσσων), not κισσός 'ivy'; the old draft's 'greenery of the pastures' came from that confusion.

choices.english: the God who had appeared to him earlier
choices.why: ἀνωτέρω 'above' points back to the ladder vision told above.

choices.term: τὸ ἀνόμοιον διὰ τὸ ἔχειν τὸ γεννητόν
choices.english: unlikeness to the Son because he is begotten
choices.why: Literally 'because he has the begotten'; the Anomoean argument from the Son's being begotten.

choices.english: the conditions of our own nature
choices.why: The results or products of created nature (birth, time); the sentence breaks off at the section's end (καὶ τά), marked '…'.
Printed line number 13 inside the Greek is page debris and is skipped.

choices.term: διαθή κης, μεγά λης, ὀφθαλ μοῖς, διαφυ λάξω, σωτηρί ας, πάν των
choices.why: Words split by line breaks in the copy-text; read as single words.
